71c9f4fe: /*
 ;This routine is used to edit the entries in the Radiology Order
 ;file (#393). It contains several entry points that are used to
 ;validate and manipulate the data associated with a radiology order.
 ;*/
f4ea2574: ;Branch to the beginning of the routine

c0fb931a: ;Set various variables used in the routine, including the file number,
 ;data location, and data delimiters. Also, check if there is existing
 ;data in the multiple field and quit if there is none.
30d9f9c1: ;If there is a DATE DICTATED value, store it in the DE(1) array.
e811c815: ;Kill the %Z variable and quit.
287f833f: ;Write the field label and colon at the appropriate screen location.
ca75a0a0: ;Quit.

ab54cbda: ;Write the field data value, and if it extends beyond a certain
 ;column, wrap to the next line.

ad4a2bc2: ;If the value is longer than 19 characters, and the DATA VALIDATION
 ;field does not contain 'I' (INTERNAL), and it contains 'F' (FREE TEXT)
 ;or 'K' (NUMERIC EXPRESSION), go to the RW^DIR2 routine.

cf6a4b77: ;If the DATA VALIDATION field contains 'I' (INTERNAL), and the DE
 ;array contains a value for the current field, display a message
 ;indicating that editing is not allowed.

a7c0343c: ;Read user input into the X variable, with a timeout specified by
 ;DTIME. If the user times out, set DTOUT and X to the up-arrow
 ;character and beep.
90f1769b: ;Quit.
78d64664: ;Kill the DQ(DQ) array element and increment DQ.
ac479649: ;Branch to the label specified by DQ.

a5edde5c: ;If the DE array contains a value for the current field, go to the
 ;PR label. Otherwise, write the field label and read user input.
071d0735: If the user does not enter a value, perform different actions based on the input variable flags.
6febe754: If the user enters a question mark, go to the question/help section.
ecc1bc63: If the user enters an '@', go to a specific routine for further processing.
7e2f18b0: If the user enters a space and there is a default value stored, display that default value.
dc574dfd: Check if the user's input matches any of the available options from the data dictionary and perform validation/transformation based on input variable settings.
3bfc55d3: Loop through each available option (piece of the 'DU' array separated by semicolons) and check if it matches the user's input.
968d7f9f: If no match is found, display the remaining unmatched part of the option line.
667996c0: If the input variable allows pointer selection, initiate the pointer lookup routine.
d5f5a2d3: If the input variable does not allow new values and the user's input exceeds the maximum length, reject the input.
c34db6df: Perform specific formatting/validation on numeric input based on the input variable settings.
e17533cf: Execute the computed 'X' code based on the current question in 'DQ'.
7d63ff0c: Store the validated user input in the 'DG' array, and if required, also store it in the LOCAL ARRAY file for future use.
61792b34: If the user's input is invalid, display an error message and go to the restart/loop section.
3509a93d: Set the input value to a standard 'BAD' response for invalid input.
a78d66bc: If the user enters a question mark followed by additional text, perform question/help processing.
